Urbice of Metz (exact dates unknown) was a prominent entrepreneur and religious figure in the Classical era.

  Born in an unknown city in a then-unknown region of the ancient world, Urbice rose to prominence through a combination of business acumen and spiritual influence.

  As a key figure in the early Christian movement, Urbice played a significant role in the spread of Christianity throughout the Roman Empire, establishing a network of churches and monasteries that would eventually span the globe.

  Urbice's legacy extends beyond his own time, as his business practices and spiritual teachings were studied and emulated by scholars and leaders for centuries to come.

  The exact date of his death remains unknown, but his impact on Western civilization continues to be felt today.

  "We must not forget the humble beginnings of our great faith," Urbice once said in a sermon to a gathering of merchants and traders, "for it is in the stories of those who came before us that we find the true meaning of our own journey."
